Threshold for immediate shutdown is 2.0 ppm, so there is an advisory window.

Spike registered at 11:47 AM local.

^pull activity logs for last 72 hours: FC-112A, FC-112B, FC-118
^cross-reference logs with scheduled defrost cycles
^if any unit attempted defrost between 10:00 AM and 1:00 PM today, hold off next scheduled defrost and switch to manual-only mode for the next 48 hours
^for unit not attempted defrost between 10:00 AM and 1:00 PM today, proceed next cycle as planned but reduce duration by 25%

Temperature at Bay 3 held steady at 34°F, so integrity of perishables confirmed.

High-value seafood shipment PO #K7B-44902 for Chef Marlon's special this weekend arrived early: 40 lbs of live scallops, 15 lbs of black cod portions, currently in Bay 4 holding at 31°F.

^move seafood shipment to Bay 3 by 3:00 PM today, but only after log pull and initial assessment on the coils
^do not commingle with existing halibut stock; lower left section of Bay 3, use upper right racks labeled "Reserved – M"
^if diagnostic shows second spike above 1.2 ppm before the move, prioritize relocate seafood shipment to backup cryo unit Receiving first, then continue coil analysis

Store manager Erica Vance notified; currently off-site until 4 PM.

^final summary to Erica Vance: include log findings, action taken on each freezer coil unit, and final location of seafood shipment
